searchText: anyone from prysm available to look at a node for me? the prysm-besu-1 node is denying engine calls due to a stale JWT token. ^ <@311971895828283393> hi <@827653956955406406> what happens if you restart besu and prysm? what does the error say? haven't tried a restart yet, will try beacon node first i think you can stand down <@311971895828283393> as i'm seeing something suspicious on besus end We were looking into this, there seems to be issues on both Besu and prysm. Besu for some reason said that a payload was INVALID and prysm errored out (there's a fix that will be up soon in our repo, sorry for the delay). The jwt issue seems to be on Besu's side cc <@827653956955406406> The "invalid payload + Prysm error'ed out" issue is unlikely the reason that is causing prysm-besu-1 node to go haywire given prysm did get an invalid respond, it just fails to prune. The jwt issue is more sus yeah, the jwt issue is gonna be a pita. there is a thread leak somewhere that is driving up contention so bad rpc methods are spanning past the token grace period. just to be clear, the INVALID response you got was correctly given by besu, just handled wrong by prysm? I just checked prysm-geth, it actually returned VALID. So I think there are two issues here: 1.) Besu returned INVALID on a payload that some other EL clients returned VALID 2.) Prysm has an issue on pruning bad block on INVALID response I only assumed 2 but it looks like 1 is also in play. For reference, this is the block at slot 34007 i don't suppose it has the same timestamp or earlier than the one at 34006 we have an outstanding issue when we treat those as INVALID instead of VALID but with a JRPC error am wondering why lighthouse/teku are ok....

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: We were looking into this, there seems to be issues on both Besu and prysm. Besu for some reason said that a payload was INVALID and prysm errored out (there's a fix that will be up soon in our repo, sorry for the delay). The jwt issue seems to be on Besu's side

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content: The "invalid payload + Prysm error'ed out" issue is unlikely the reason that is causing prysm-besu-1 node to go haywire given prysm did get an invalid respond, it just fails to prune. The jwt issue is more sus

excerpts.author: robocopsgonemad
excerpts.content: yeah, the jwt issue is gonna be a pita. there is a thread leak somewhere that is driving up contention so bad rpc methods are spanning past the token grace period.

excerpts.author: robocopsgonemad
excerpts.content: just to be clear, the INVALID response you got was correctly given by besu, just handled wrong by prysm?

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content:
I just checked prysm-geth, it actually returned VALID. So I think there are two issues here:

1.) Besu returned INVALID on a payload that some other EL clients returned VALID
2.) Prysm has an issue on pruning bad block on INVALID response

I only assumed 2 but it looks like 1 is also in play. For reference, this is the block at slot 34007
